newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-ITALY SHOCK SPAIN WITH DAVIS CUP TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ITALY SHOCK SPAIN WITH DAVIS CUP TRIUMPH.

text.p: Unfancied Italy dumped Spain out of the Davis Cup on Saturday by snatching an unassailable 3-0 lead in their world group quarter-final tie.
Omar Camporese and Diego Nargiso collapsed onto the indoor court in an exhausted embrace after a three-hour 5-7 7-6 (7-0) 6-2 7-6 (7-5) victory over Javier Sanchez and Francisco Roig.
"These have been two fantastic days," said non-playing captain Adriano Panatta, who was raised shoulder-high by team officials to cheers from the 5,000 strong Italian crowd.
"I am happy for them and I'm happy for myself. The semi-final is a great goal and we've reached it two years running. Now we're going to rest a bit," he said.
Italy were knocked out of the last four by France last year and went into the tie in Pesaro, on the Adriatic holiday coast, talking down their chances of victory.
Spain fielded two players in the world's top 12 and had been highly favoured to win the tie.

On Friday, Camporese, ranked 156th, came from two sets down to beat ninth-ranked Carlos Moya in the opening singles while Italian number one Renzo Furlan overcame Albert Costa, ranked 12th, in another five-setter.
The teams will play two dead reverse singles matches on Sunday.
Italy face either Sweden or South Africa in the semifinal. Sweden led South Africa 2-1 after Saturday's doubles.
